# Prepare an input file with *File Builder*

IMPORTANT NOTE: if you are using the BCG results, your data should be
collected and processed using these field and laboratory protocols
[<a href="https://github.com/Blocktt/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/blob/main/inst/apps/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/www/links/Methods_Bugs_Fish_20260525.pdf" target="_blank">PDF</a>].

-   Macroinvertebrates: USGS National Water‑Quality Assessment (NAWQA)
    Richest Targeted Habitat (RTH) method

-   Fish: composite of two electrofishing passes - one through
    deep-water areas with a boat or tow barge; the second through
    shallower riffle areas with a backpack electrofisher

[**Step 1: Create the input file**]{.underline}

The input file must be a comma-separated file (CSV). It can include data
for multiple samples, sites and Index Classes.

**REQUIRED fields. Column heading names in the input file are flexible
(use drop-down menus to match).**

```{r table_req}
# Packages
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Data
fn <- "Requirements.xlsx"
path <- file.path("files", fn)
df <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Req_Fields")

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
df %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")
```

[Index Classes]{.underline}:

-   Main_BarberPool

-   Main_Eckert

-   Main_VetGlen

-   Main_SoChannel

-   Main_Middleton

-   Main_NotusParma

Sites can be matched with the appropriate class/stream segment using
these geospatial (shapefile and kmz) files
<a href="https://github.com/Blocktt/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/blob/main/inst/apps/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/www/links/BCG_ClassSegments2_20260304.zip" target="_blank">[ZIP]</a>.

[**Step 2: Go to the 'Import File' tab and upload the input
file**]{.underline}

[**Step 3: Go to the 'Prepare Input File' tab and run File
Builder**]{.underline}

The File Builder joins the taxon name in the input file with the
‘Taxon_orig’ column in the Taxa Translator table and performs two
functions:

-   Translates the original taxon name to the proper Operational
    Taxonomic Unit (OTU) for the BCG calculation.

-   Adds in new columns with taxa attributes and hierarchy (e.g., Order,
    Family) that are needed for the metric calculations.

The Lower Boise River fish and macroinvertebrate
<a href="https://github.com/leppott/BioMonTools_SupportFiles/tree/main/data/taxa_official/LowerBoise" target="_blank">Taxa
Translator and Taxa Attribute tables</a> are available online.

When the File Builder has finished running, **a prompt box will
appear**. It will notify you if your File Builder run was successful or
failed. Or, in some cases (e.g., if there are problems with your input
file), the screen will gray out (meaning the Shiny app has crashed) and
you’ll have to refresh the app, investigate potential problems with your
input file, and try again.

If your run was successful, the prompt box will alert you if there are
taxa in your input file that don’t match with the taxa list in the Taxa
Translator table.

**What if there are non-matching taxa?** Open the
‘BCG_TaxaTranslator_nonmatches’ file and view the list of non-matching
taxa. If the non-matches are due to a misspelling, extra space or other
small issue, fix the non-matching taxa in your input file, re-upload the
file via the ‘Import File’ tab, and rerun the File Builder (and to
prevent confusion, delete the first set of output files with the
non-matching taxa). If the non-matching taxa are legitimate taxa that
need to be added to the Taxa Translator table, notify Jen Stamp
([Jen.Stamp\@tetratech.com](mailto:Jen.Stamp@tetratech.com)) and Tetra
Tech will update the Taxa Translator table as soon as resources permit.

[**Step 4: Download and unzip the results**]{.underline}

**A ‘results’ folder will appear, with the following subfolders:**

```{r table_FB_folders}
# Packages
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Data
fn <- "OutputFileSubtabs.xlsx"
path <- file.path("files", fn)
df <- read_excel(path, sheet = "FileBuild_Folders")

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
df %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")
```

**In the results subfolders, there will be four File Builder output
files, described below.**

```{r table_FB_files}
# Packages
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Data
fn <- "OutputFileSubtabs.xlsx"
path <- file.path("files", fn)
df <- read_excel(path, sheet = "FileBuild_Files")

options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
df %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")
```

**Download METADATA**
<a href="https://github.com/Blocktt/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/blob/main/inst/apps/LowerBoiseBCGCalc/www/links/Metadata_FileBuilder_20260526.zip" target="_blank">[ZIP]</a>
for all the File Builder output files.
